entities.summary: Wawrzyniec, also known as Lawrence, was a medieval Bishop of Wrocław, Poland in the years 1207–1232. He played a significant role in the Gdańsk Diocese and was a key figure in the Catholic Church during this period. Lawrence was also involved in the governance of the region and was known for his administrative skills. His legacy continued through the centuries, with the city of Wrocław remaining an important center of Catholicism. The city's cathedral, built during his tenure, remains a testament to his influence. Lawrence's significance lies in his role as a mediator between the nobility and the clergy, and his efforts to promote religious education and reform. He is remembered for his contributions to the growth of the Catholic Church in Poland and his dedication to the welfare of his flock. Lawrence's life and legacy have been the subject of various historical accounts, with many considering him an important figure in the history of the Gdańsk Diocese. The Polish historian Jan Długosz wrote that Lawrence was a 'man of great wisdom and piety', who was ' beloved by all who knew him'.
